newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends off but near high as spreads hold.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends off but near high as spreads hold.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended lower on Tuesday under pressure from the prospect of another build in U.S. heating oil stocks and a sloppy European diesel market, dealers said.
But increased trade interest in the nearby intermonth spreads trimmed losses on the prompt Nov contract, they added.
"The spreads came in strong and we've moved back up towards the highs on those," said a broker.
Nov gas oil closed at $208.50 a tonne, 50 cents down on the day and only 50 cents off the session high. Dec lost $1.00 to close at $204.25.
Dealers said Brent was stuck within a relatively tight 25-cent range with many players sitting out ahead of the release of the latest U.S. inventory data due later on Tuesday.
"There's a lot of speculation (ahead of the APIs) and that's one of the reasons why there's not a lot of volume on Brent today," said a broker.
Dec Brent gained 13 cents at $22.41 a barrel by 1745 GMT.
Traders are forecasting the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a distillate inventory build of about 1.5 million to two million barrels in its stocks report for the week ended November 1.
European physical diesel markets were under pressure from the arrival of U.S. and Algerian cargoes, traders said.

Crude dealers shrugged off news of a successful seven-hour heart surgery operation on Russian President Boris Yeltsin and were equally unmoved by signs OPEC would not raise its quotas at the next meeting.
Iranian oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Tuesday he did not believe that there was a need for OPEC countries to raise their output ceiling during talks in Vienna later this month.
